topics: Concept of effective communication and communication skills
Level of communication: upward and downward
Types of communication: verbal, non-verbal and visual
Types of communication: interpersonal, intrapersonal, extra personal and mass
Parts of speech: noun, verb, pronoun, adjective, adverb, preposition, conjunction, interjection
Tenses: present simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous
Tenses: past simple, continuous and perfect; future simple
Modal auxiliaries: can, could, may, might, must, shall, will, should, would, ought to, need
Basic sentence patterns of English: SV, SVO, SVA, SVC
Short story: After Twenty Years - O. Henry
Poetry: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening - Robert Frost
Email writing: format and types (inquiry, reply to inquiry, order, complaint)
Paragraph topics: festivals, nature and environment, famous personalities, favourite sports, friends and family members

course_outcomes: CO1: Use strategies to minimize barriers of effective communication.
CO3: Develop reading and listening skills in terms of fluency and comprehensibility.
CO4: Compose different types of written communication.
CO5: Communicate orally in a given situation with a purpose.
source_note: Syllabus text transcribed from the uploaded GTU DI01000031 PDF (Communication Skills in English, Semester 1, HSMC-1). Unit hours, weightages, the 70 + 30 + 20 + 30 marks split and the course outcomes are copied from it.

official_practicals.outcome: Listening to recorded lectures, poems, interviews and speeches
Use antonyms and synonyms effectively in oral and written forms
Communicate ideas effectively and fluently in oral and written communication
Articulate vowels, consonants and diphthongs correctly
Speak with appropriate intonation, voice modulation, pitch, speed and volume
Deliver a presentation effectively in the class
Communicate effectively through verbal and non-verbal means
Practice online exercises for listening and reading comprehension
